referents.why: First person common singular 'my' (of soul) in a psalm is the psalm's own voice; no other speaker is quoted in this verse.
referents.category: first person in the psalm's own voice

referents.why: First person common singular 'me', object of 'guides' in clause 1; same psalm voice, no speech by another.
referents.category: first person in the psalm's own voice

referents.why: Third masculine singular suffix on 'name' (his name), the name of the one who guides, i.e. the LORD named in verse 1; no other masculine singular candidate fits the sake-of-name clause.
referents.category: possessive pronoun for the divine name

referents.why: Implied third masculine singular subject of a yiqtol (he restores); the act is the shepherd's, and the nearest agreeing doer is the LORD of verse 1.
referents.category: implied subject of a yiqtol line in the psalm

referents.why: Implied third masculine singular subject of a yiqtol (he guides me), the same agent as the preceding line; the nearest agreeing doer is the LORD of verse 1.
referents.category: implied subject of a yiqtol line in the psalm

groups.why: Verse 3 is a bicolon with no conjunction: the second line restates the first line's roles (agent and object of the same act of shepherding) without a subject of its own, because the subject is the same LORD.

none_fit.where: cl1, 'for the sake of His name' (lamed + ma'an + name)
none_fit.what: a purpose given as a noun phrase, not a clause; the purpose link takes a clause or command as its destination, so the purpose cannot be linked to the name
